$comment: DSH wire contract extracted from the published npm packages. Every method/event carries a file:line `source`. `confidence: low` marks anything inferred rather than read verbatim.

meta.versionCorrection: The task brief named client-connection@0.2.0-rc.2. The package actually on disk is 0.0.1-rc.1; all citations below refer to the real on-disk files.

basePath.note: Prefix route: owns /api and /api/<anything>. Registered once by the node half.

surfaces.name: A. ApiProxy typed unary RPC
surfaces.description: Dotted method names, POST /api/<method>. This is the surface every browser/mobile client uses.

surfaces.name: B. Generic Connection RPC channel (TypeRT Remotes)
surfaces.description: Slashed endpoint names on the same /api channel, POST /api/<ns>/<method>. Used by the gateway for Remote dispatch and streaming remotes.
surfaces.note: Wire framing is verified; the concrete endpoint list is taken from the controller .d.ts files and the goal endpoints appear only in the client fixture.

unaryRequest.pathDerivation: callUnary hardcodes the literal '/api/' prefix; the method string is NOT taken from the body.

rpcId.note: opaque echo token, minted client-side via crypto.randomUUID(); no length constraint

method.note: MUST equal the path endpoint or the server returns bad-request

payload.note: left wide on the wire; second-level parse is dispatched per method

rpcId.note: client MUST verify this equals its own rpcId
MUST equal the rpcId of the server-pushed frame being answered

responseEndpoints.description: Server-initiated RPC answers (approvals, user questions) travel back over this single endpoint, NOT over the WebSockets.

wireForms.note: Exactly four full forms, discriminated on `type`.

httpStatusCodes.meaning: envelope delivered; business outcome is inside result.ok
forbidden — trust fence refused, or a privileged method from a non-loopback authority
not found — wrong method (not POST) or unmatched path
upgrade required — GET on an event path

clientSideBehaviour.non2xx: throws Error(`transport failure for ${path}: HTTP ${status}`) — transport faults are NOT RpcResults
clientSideBehaviour.rpcIdMismatch: throws Error(`rpcId mismatch for ${method}: sent X, got Y`)

timeoutPolicy.default: AbortSignal.timeout(30000), merged with any caller signal via AbortSignal.any

requestSizeLimit.note: When an `attachments` service is present, the cap must be >= ceil(maxMessageImageBytes * 4/3) + 1MiB or plugin activation throws.

websockets.direction: server-to-client only; client->server frames are a protocol violation
websockets.subprotocolNote: WebSocketServer is constructed with { noServer: true } and no handleProtocols option — clients MUST NOT send a Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header.

framing.transport: one RFC6455 text frame per event
framing.binaryFramesRejected: client drops non-string frames as 'binary WebSocket frame'

frameShape.rpcId: string — HOST-MINTED per frame; for answerable pushes (approval/requested, question/requested) it is STABLE across reconnects and is the token you echo to /api/respond; pure pushes mint a fresh id each time

framing.clientSideParsing: serverRequestSchema.parse(JSON.parse(data)) then frameSchema.parse(full.payload) — a frame failing either level is logged and dropped; the stream survives

openPayload.note: No query string, no subscribe filter. The host opens the stream with payload {} as soon as the socket upgrades.

behaviour.anyClientMessage: server closes with code 1008, reason 'downlink only'
behaviour.streamEnd: a stream/error frame, then the socket is closed by the server
behaviour.upgradeRejected: raw HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden with body 'forbidden' written straight to the socket (no WebSocket close frame)

reconnect.policy: client-owned; the protocol mandates reconnection, it does not implement it

reference.backoff: min(10000, 500 * 2^(attempt-1)), then randomized: cap/2 + random*(cap/2) — i.e. 50%-100% jittered

readinessHandshake.description: A connection is only declared 'connected' once BOTH sockets have opened AND host.describe has succeeded, within streamOpenTimeoutMs (3000ms). Any failure aborts the generation and retries.
readinessHandshake.note: A native client MUST replay its RPC state after reconnect: approvals and questions are re-pushed with the SAME rpcId while unanswered.

reconnect.replayGuarantee: Resident pending approvals/questions are replayed on every mux open with the same rpcId, matching host replay semantics.

sseAlternative.note: The non-browser AbstractApiClient base reads the SAME two paths as text/event-source ('\n\n' framing, 'data: ' lines) instead of upgrading. Only relevant if you target the in-process carrier.

authentication.statement: There is NO authentication layer. No tokens, no cookies, no Authorization header, no API key, no session credentials are read or required anywhere on the /api surface.
authentication.sourceQuote: The fence is a reachability policy, not authentication; the Web carrier provides no authentication layer.

whatTheFenceChecks.name: isTrustedApiRequest(request, trustedHosts)

orderedRules.rule: Host header must be present and WHATWG-parsable
Host hostname is loopback (localhost, [::1], or 127.0.0.0/8) OR matches a trustedHosts entry
sec-fetch-site, when present, must not be 'cross-site'
Origin, when present, must equal the Host authority exactly; absent Origin passes

trustedHostMatching.withPort: exact host:port match after WHATWG normalization

whatTheFenceChecks.rejects: HTTP 403 'forbidden' before any RPC dispatch; upgrade refused before any stream starts

privilegedMethods.note: These 15 methods pass the fence with an EMPTY trust list, so even a trusted-host deployment only reaches them over loopback.

authentication.nativeClientImplication: Any native app that can reach the socket owns the entire API. Combined with default loopback binding this is the only real control: the deployment binds 127.0.0.1 by default. A --host 0.0.0.0 deployment with trustedHosts grants an unauthenticated LAN caller 38 of the 53 methods.

methods.name: session.list
methods.description: List sessions, newest-updated first; cursor paginates.

methods.name: session.search
methods.description: Full-text session search; snippet capped at 240 Unicode code points.

methods.name: session.create
methods.description: Create a session. workspaceId and cwd are mutually exclusive.

methods.name: session.history
methods.returns: SessionHistoryValue { events: HistoryEntry[], hasMore: boolean, projections? }
methods.description: Page the session event journal backwards; the projections baseline rides only the tail page.

methods.name: session.models
methods.returns: SessionModelsValue { current, routable: boolean, groups, failures }
methods.description: Current model selection plus the routable catalog and per-provider load failures.

methods.name: session.selectModel
methods.description: Pin the session to an exact provider/model pair.

methods.name: session.rename
methods.description: Set the session title; returns the normalized title and its event seq.

methods.name: session.fork
methods.description: Fork a session from a given sequence (or its head).

methods.name: session.prompt
methods.returns: SessionPromptValue { accepted: true, command?: { kind: 'success', text? } }
methods.description: Submit a turn. mode=queue enqueues behind the running turn; mode=steer injects into it. The command slot appears only when the text dispatched a slash command.

methods.name: session.attachment
methods.description: Fetch a durable image attachment by id; data is a base64 payload sized against maxMessageImageBytes.

methods.name: session.updateQueue
methods.description: Edit, remove, or promote-to-steer one queued inbox item.

methods.name: session.cancel
methods.description: Cancel the running turn.

methods.name: subagent.list
methods.description: List a parent's child subagents, including unhealthy diagnostics rows.

methods.name: subagent.history
methods.description: Page a child subagent's journal.

methods.name: subagent.prompt
methods.description: Send a follow-up turn to a continuable child subagent.

methods.name: subagent.interrupt
methods.description: Interrupt a running continuable child subagent.

methods.name: host.describe
methods.returns: HostDescription { version, cwd, provider?, model?, attachedSessions }
methods.description: Host version, cwd, active model, attached session count. Doubles as the connection readiness handshake — call it before trusting the event streams.

methods.name: host.pickDirectory
methods.description: Open the native directory picker on the host machine; null means the user cancelled. LOOPBACK-ONLY and caller-paced (no built-in timeout).

methods.name: host.listDirectory
methods.returns: DirectoryListing { path, home, crumbs: DirectoryEntry[], entries: DirectoryEntry[], truncated: boolean }
methods.description: List a host directory with breadcrumbs; omitted path starts at the host default.

methods.name: host.createDirectory

params.name: name
params.type: string (single non-blank segment, no / or \, not . or ..)

methods.description: Create one directory; returns its absolute path.

methods.name: host.openPath
methods.description: Reveal/open a path on the host desktop. LOOPBACK-ONLY (acts on the host machine).

methods.name: workspace.list
methods.description: List workspaces and the current archive set.

methods.name: workspace.create
methods.description: Create (or attach to) a workspace at a host path; created=false when it already existed.

methods.name: workspace.rename
methods.description: Rename a workspace title.

methods.name: workspace.delete
methods.description: Delete a workspace.

methods.name: workspace.insertSessionBefore
methods.description: Move/reorder a session within a workspace; omitting beforeSessionId moves it to the head.

methods.name: workspace.archiveSession
methods.description: Archive a session; returns the complete updated archive set.

methods.name: command.list
methods.description: List the slash commands available to a session.

methods.name: command.execute
methods.description: Pure admission only — outcomes arrive later as logged lifecycle events correlated by commandId. Caller-paced (no timeout).

methods.name: skill.list
methods.description: List skills visible to a session.

methods.name: agentPreset.list
methods.returns: { presets: AgentPresetEntry[], authorable: boolean, hasDocument: boolean }
methods.description: List agent presets with trust level and default flag. Not loopback-gated.

methods.name: agentPreset.select
methods.description: Bind a session to a preset. Not loopback-gated.

methods.name: agentPreset.read
methods.description: Read a preset's composition text. LOOPBACK-ONLY — a composition names the plugins a session runs, so reading is reconnaissance.

methods.name: agentPreset.copy
methods.description: Copy a preset to a new user-trust id (the only authoring write). LOOPBACK-ONLY.

methods.name: agentPreset.openDocument
methods.returns: { opened: true } | { opened: false, path: string }
methods.description: Open the preset document; when not a document it returns the path instead. LOOPBACK-ONLY.

methods.name: agentPreset.remove
methods.description: Delete a user preset. LOOPBACK-ONLY.

methods.name: goal.create
methods.description: Create a persisted goal. Mutation-only: every value is just a ref acknowledgement — current goal state travels exclusively on the 'goal' session projection.

methods.name: goal.edit
methods.description: Edit a goal; at least one of objective / maxGoalRounds is required.

methods.name: goal.pause
methods.description: Pause an active goal.

methods.name: goal.resume
methods.description: Resume a paused goal.

methods.name: goal.complete
methods.description: Mark a goal complete.

methods.name: goal.clear
methods.description: Clear the goal entirely (the only non-ref value).

methods.name: settings.describe
methods.returns: { writable: boolean, hasDocument: boolean, namespaces: SettingsNamespaceView[] }
methods.description: Describe every exposed settings namespace with redacted secrets. LOOPBACK-ONLY (returns the full exposed configuration).

methods.name: settings.openDocument
methods.description: Open the settings document on the host desktop. LOOPBACK-ONLY.

methods.name: settings.update
methods.description: Shallow-merge a patch into a namespace. optimistic-concurrency via expectedRevision; mismatch yields settings-conflict. LOOPBACK-ONLY.

methods.name: settings.replace
methods.description: Replace one section wholesale. LOOPBACK-ONLY.

methods.name: settings.mutate
methods.description: Apply path-addressed set/unset edits atomically. LOOPBACK-ONLY.

methods.name: credentials.describe
methods.description: Probe which credential refs are configured and their source. LOOPBACK-ONLY — arbitrary env-var probing is reconnaissance.

methods.name: credentials.set
methods.description: Write a secret into the host store. LOOPBACK-ONLY.

methods.name: credentials.unset
methods.description: Remove a stored secret. LOOPBACK-ONLY.

methods.name: llm.providers
methods.description: List configurable LLM providers. Deliberately NOT loopback-gated — no endpoints or key state.

methods.name: llm.models
methods.description: Global model catalog grouped by provider, with per-provider load failures.

methods.name: llm.discoverModels
methods.description: Make the HOST issue a GET to a caller-chosen URL and report back models or an error. LOOPBACK-ONLY — it is an SSRF probe for anything the host can reach but the browser cannot.

remoteMethods.comment: SECOND wire surface. Generic Connection RPC on the same /api channel with SLASHED endpoints (POST /api/<ns>/<method>), dispatched through the TypeRT gateway. Envelope shape is identical to surface A. Verified from the controllers' generated remote maps; the goal endpoints are fixture-only.
remoteMethods.transportNote: rpc.call(channel, endpoint, payload) mints its own rpcId, POSTs {type:'client-request',rpcId,method:endpoint,payload} to `${channel}/${endpoint}`, and returns result after verifying the rpcId echo.
remoteMethods.endpointPattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9_$.-]+$ per slash-separated segment; empty, '.' and '..' segments rejected

goalsUnverified.name: goals/create
goalsUnverified.note: Appears ONLY inside the client-side fixture carrier. No server-side registration found in the downloaded packages.

responseEndpoints.name: /api/respond (approval)
responseEndpoints.params: RpcResult<{ approvalId: string, outcome: 'allowed-once' | 'rejected' }>, sent as { type: 'client-response', rpcId: <the frame's rpcId>, result }
responseEndpoints.description: Answer a tool-approval prompt. The rpcId is HOST-MINTED and stable while the approval is unanswered. A not-ok result resolves the request as cancelled.

responseEndpoints.name: /api/respond (question)
responseEndpoints.params: RpcResult<QuestionResponse>, sent as { type: 'client-response', rpcId: <the frame's rpcId>, result } — payload shape UNVERIFIED
responseEndpoints.description: Answer an ask-user question prompt. Result outcome maps to question/resolved outcome 'answered' when ok and 'cancelled' when not ok.
responseEndpoints.note: QuestionResponsePayload is exported as a type (cc/types/client/api.d.ts:1) but its zod schema is NOT in the bundled schema regions and no server implementation was available. Infer its field names from AskUserQuestionItemSchema (cc/client.js:5466-5480) at your own risk.

events.name: session/event

payload.name: event
payload.type: SessionEvent { type: string, seq: int>=0, time: number, data: unknown, sourceEventSeqs?: number[], surfaceOp?: unknown }

events.description: One durable session journal event. The workhorse of the whole UI.

events.name: session/subscribed
events.description: Confirms the session journal subscription and its current head seq — use it to detect a gap after reconnect.

events.name: approval/requested
events.description: A tool needs human approval. ANSWERABLE: send a client-response to /api/respond using this frame's rpcId.

events.name: approval/resolved
events.description: An approval reached a terminal outcome (possibly decided by another client).

events.name: question/requested
events.description: The agent is asking the user questions. ANSWERABLE via /api/respond using this frame's rpcId.

events.name: question/resolved
events.description: A question prompt reached a terminal outcome.

events.name: session/queue
events.description: Full transient queue state for a session (not a delta).

events.name: session/projection
events.description: One derived projection key changed. Key 'goal' carries the current goal state.

events.name: stream/error
events.description: Terminal stream failure. The pump breaks out of its loop on this and the socket is closed — reconnect.

events.name: host/session-added
events.description: A session appeared.

events.name: host/session-removed
events.description: A session disappeared.

events.name: host/session-status
events.description: A session started or stopped running.

events.name: host/agent-error
events.description: A session's agent failed with a human-readable message.

events.name: host/workspace-changed
events.description: A workspace was created, renamed or reordered.

events.name: host/workspace-removed
events.description: A workspace was deleted.

events.name: host/archived-sessions-changed
events.description: The complete archive set changed.

events.name: host/commands-changed
events.description: The slash-command roster changed; re-fetch command.list.

events.name: host/session-preset-changed
events.description: A session's agent preset binding changed.

events.name: host/settings-changed
events.description: A settings namespace changed on disk; re-fetch settings.describe.

events.name: host/credentials-changed

events.name: host/models-changed
events.description: The model catalog changed; re-fetch session.models or llm.models.

events.name: stream/error
events.description: Terminal host-stream failure; the socket closes and must be reconnected.

gaps.evidence: No string literal matching "job.*", "terminal.*" or "account.*" exists anywhere in the six downloaded packages. These domains do not exist in this wire contract.

Exported as a type (cc/types/client/api.d.ts:1) but its zod definition is absent from every bundled schema region and the server-side /api/respond pending table lives in @deepseek-ai/dsh-host-apiproxy, which was not downloaded.

gaps.item: Server-side /api/respond routing and the pending table
gaps.evidence: cc/index.js:545 delegates every unmatched /api request to the apiProxy service; the pending-table implementation is in the undownloaded apiproxy package. Only the client contract and a fixture simulation (cc/client.js:9561-9597) were available.
Found only in the client-side fixture carrier (cc/client.js:9604-9612). No server registration is present in the downloaded packages, and the payload envelope { args: {...} } is fixture-specific.

AbstractApiClient reads the same two paths as SSE (cc/client.js:6162-6168); WebApiClient overrides with a real WebSocket upgrade (cc/client.js:9777-9782). A native client should use the WebSocket path.

cc/client.js:5186 declares data as unknown(); the durable core is merge-extensible and carries an unknown-type branch at the union level. Per-event data shapes are NOT in the connection package — they live in dsh-session/types and dsh-client-ui-chat, which expose only view types.
cc/client.js:5816-5817 declare schema and value as unknown(); the namespace schema is host-supplied at runtime.

gaps.item: Stream framing for session/control, session/follow, workspace/follow
gaps.evidence: These are RemoteStreamHandle endpoints (sc/typert.remote-client.d.ts:44, :46; wc/typert.remote-client.d.ts:36). Their frame unions and wire framing live in the apiproxy/gateway packages, which were not downloaded.
